1c71s8n:202: In traditional software development, code paths are deterministic—given the same input, the same code always produces the same output, and tests can precisely verify expected behavior. 3qygz0:212: Human evaluation captures semantic, intent, and creative quality dimensions that are hard for machines to quantify, but it does not scale, is costly, and is not repeatable. Code-based evaluation is fast, low-cost, and deterministic, but it can only detect structural attributes (JSON validity, keyword presence, length constraints) and cannot assess semantic correctness—"you can check whether the output contains refund, but you cannot tell whether the output correctly explains the refund policy." LLM-as-a-Judge can handle semantic quality judgments but requires calibration to human preferences and may share blind spots with the application LLM. The three methods complement one another and are all indispensable.

ap3p5q:165: Traditional evaluation requires predefined "correct answers," which works on closed test sets but cannot be applied to live traffic—production data has an open distribution, so it is impossible to prepare reference answers for all possible inputs in advance. Reference-free evaluators assess only the output's own quality attributes (such as format correctness, reasonableness of length, and whether harmless requests are refused). They can run on production traffic in real time to confirm whether deployed model behavior matches the experiment phase, enabling true production quality drift detection.
k1gez4:208: This loop connects production (trace tracking, online monitoring) with the development stage (dataset management, experiment evaluation, CI gates), and new data generated by each release flows back into the next round of improvement. This means AI quality evaluation is not a one-time effort but a continuously operated systems engineering task—the failure modes captured by evals generate new training data, better training data improves the model, the improved model brings new behavior patterns, and those new patterns create new failure modes for evals to capture. The smoother this flywheel turns, the more efficient the AI system's quality improvement becomes.
